paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The graph compares the loss over training time between the vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM model. The x-axis represents training time in seconds, ranging from 0 to 250,000, with major gridlines at intervals of 50,000. The y-axis shows the loss value, ranging from 2.40 to 2.75, with major gridlines at intervals of 0.05. Two lines are plotted: the vanilla Transformer (purple, with triangle markers and a solid line) and SepLLM (red, with circle markers and a solid line). Both models show a decreasing trend in loss as training time increases. The vanilla Transformer starts at a loss of approximately 2.75 and decreases to about 2.51 by 250,000 seconds. SepLLM starts at a slightly lower loss of around 2.70 and decreases to approximately 2.49 by the end of the training period. A green dashed horizontal line at a loss of 2.50 is shown, with a vertical green dashed line at approximately 200,000 seconds indicating the point where SepLLM's loss reaches 2.50. A green bracket and text "1.26×" indicate that SepLLM reaches this loss level in 1.26 times less training time compared to the vanilla Transformer. The legend in the top right corner identifies the two models.
